built.selftest_output:
FIX: run_m4.py: merge_capsid_and_pose took every atom of the docking tool's pose file and relabelled it as the receptor chain. That file holds the whole complex, so the merged structure carried the capsid twice: once from the pair's own structure and once from the pose, under the receptor's chain letter. On the failed launch this gave a chain of 592 residues with repeated residue numbers where 94 were expected. The fix takes from the pose only the atoms of the pair's receptor chain, falling back to the pose chains that are not capsid chains.
FIX: run_m4.py: the merged structure's chain ends carried no second acid oxygen (OXT), so the force field had no template for them and building the solvated complex stopped. This is the error in tool_logs/md_build_pair1_1.log: 'No template found for residue 686 (VAL). The set of atoms matches VAL, but the bonds are different.' Residue 686 is the last residue of capsid chain B, valine 387, a chain cut out of the crystal structure. New functions terminal_oxygen and cap_chain_ends add that oxygen to the last residue of every chain, 1.25 angstrom from the backbone carbon and pointing away from the other two bonded atoms; a chain that already ends with it, such as chain A at residue 735, is left alone.
FIX: run_m4.py: added _selftest_md_complex to the selftest, covering both fixes.

Local checks, all that the directive names, all run in this directory:
  python3 -m py_compile run_m4.py -> ok
  bash -n onbox_m4.sh -> ok
  python3 run_m4.py --selftest -> 'selftest: PASS', exit 0

What the new selftest checks: a planted pair of two capsid chains and one receptor chain, with a pose file holding the capsid 100 angstrom away and the receptor 50 angstrom away. The merged structure must hold 9, 5 and 5 atoms in the three chains, no atom from the pose's capsid copy, the receptor at its docked position, an acid oxygen on the last residue of each of the three chains and none on a residue inside a chain. The oxygen must sit 1.25 angstrom from the backbone carbon, carry element O and its residue's name, and point away from the other oxygen. A residue that already holds the oxygen gets no second one, and a residue missing a backbone atom is left alone.

Checked against the files the failed launch left behind, rebuilding its first complex with the patched function: one capsid copy, 4143 plus 1369 atoms, and the receptor at 726 atoms, 6238 in all, against 11747 before; every chain contiguous; acid oxygens added at chain B residue 387 and chain R residue 237 and not at chain A residue 735, which already had one; oxygen to carbon 1.2500 angstrom and oxygen to oxygen 2.1446 angstrom; every residue name standard; the receptor displaced up to 13.776 angstrom from the undocked structure, so it is the docked copy.

REPORT, not patched, because the directive forbids touching the measurement protocol: with the duplicated capsid gone the complexes are about 6200 to 7700 atoms across 123 to 156 angstrom. The water padding rule's floor of 8 angstrom then gives a box of roughly 290,000 to 300,000 atoms, above the 120,000 to 180,000 range, and the one rebuild cannot go below the floor. If that estimate holds on the box, the dynamics input (C2) will be VOID for its atom count with the raw count kept, by the rule as written. Widening the range or lowering the floor would change the protocol, so I changed neither. The gate should decide whether it wants a launch on that footing.
built.expected:
Wall clock, one launch, outer limit 7200 s, start of the parent script plus 30 s as time zero. Environment activation and lock check under 60 s. Capability check 60 to 180 s. Downloads and parameter extraction 300 to 900 s, or near zero when the archive is reused. Controls 65 to 75 s. Anchor, serial then parallel then diagnostics, 300 to 900 s. Per-pair docking and analysis 300 to 600 s, at most 250 s per pair. AlphaFold timings 1200 to 2000 s. Dynamics 600 to 1600 s, at most 600 s per complex. Storage under 60 s. Endpoints under 100 s. On the last launch the run reached the dynamics stage at about 1600 s elapsed, so the stages after it have room.

Records, 13 files: one per input (C1 to C4), the anchor record, the environment check record, the three control records (60 s sleep, empty run, unit and scale), the run validity file, the summary with its compute table, the finished marker and the compute table file. Raw rows, one line per unit: 3 or more AlphaFold runs over 3 pairs and 3 seeds, up to 9; 2 anchor docking rows; 3 pair docking rows; up to 3 dynamics rows; 2 control rows; 1 or more storage rows. Supporting files: the pair evidence file, 3 FASTA files, 3 pair structures, the entry 6IHB structure, 5 rank tables with their poses, the reporter file and trajectory size record per complex, the download record, the marker record, the environment listing and the tool logs.

Outcome, on the evidence of the last two launches: the anchor misses its tolerance again, by the owner's ruling it stays a miss, so the run is void from the anchor onward, every later record carries that and the run exits 4 unless a worse row applies. The auxiliary hours (C3) should be decided as before. The dynamics and storage inputs (C2, C4) now get past the failure that stopped them, but see the atom-count note in the selftest field: C2 may still be VOID by the range rule, and C4 then loses its dynamics artifact type and is VOID too. Cost at 1.99 USD per hour: about 3.98 USD for a full 7200 s, within the 5 USD launch budget and the 13.32 USD left of the 20 USD cap.
